Resume one paused run on your own workflow account. What it does next has no spending limit from this call.
Send a signal with arguments to one run on your own workflow account. Accepted means the run recorded it; what your workers do with it is up to them.

On your own workflow account: send a signal to the open run with your workflow key, starting it first when none is open. Returns a ref for the workflow.execution.* calls. Accepted means the signal was recorded, not that your workers handled it.
Read one execution span; requested message text may contain personal data.
Request that an execution stop. Requires confirmation and approval; earlier effects cannot be undone.
Add tags to an execution, refusing more than ten unique tags in total.
Force-end one run on your own workflow account at once: no cleanup code runs. Pass confirm: true and an idempotency key. Not a cancellation request; there is no undo. Its history stays readable.
Read an execution trace with bounded spans and explicit truncation. Requested messages may contain personal data.

Send an update to one run on your own workflow account and wait for it to be accepted or finished (up to about 20 seconds). Returns a ref for workflow.execution.update-result. Pass an idempotency key: a retry with it never applies the update twice.
Read the outcome of an update sent with workflow.execution.update on your own workflow account, optionally waiting up to 20 seconds for it to finish. Never sends the update again.
Count the runs on your own connected workflow namespace, filtered by state, workflow type and start time, optionally per state.
List execution metadata with workflow, status and start-time filters.
Search execution metadata by explicit account-compatible filters.
Get workflow metadata. Graph fields may be omitted; executable parameters and credentials are never returned.
List workflow metadata in your connected account.
List workflow log metadata without inputs, outputs, authors or change payloads. Credits describe consumption in your connected account.
Describe the workflow namespace your connection points at: its state, history retention and switched-on features, plus its account configuration when the connection has an account management key.
List the workflow namespaces on your own account (with an account management key on the connection), or the ones your namespace endpoint can see.
List the organization bound to your connected workflow account.
List projects in the organization bound to your workflow connection.
Read a queue and its current workload.
Restore the concurrency defined in code; increasing concurrency may start queued work.
Override queue concurrency. Raising the limit can start queued code and incur account charges.
Pause or resume a queue. Resuming may start code and incur account charges; running executions are unaffected.
List queues in your connected environment, with at most 100 rows per page.
Start a named workflow in your account. This may execute code and incur downstream charges; acceptance does not mean completion.

Start up to 10 named workflows as one native batch job, with at most 1 MiB of JSON total. Each result carries your row id and confirmed execution id; acceptance does not mean completion. Your account pays compute and downstream charges.
Enable future scheduled code execution and account charges.
Create a managed schedule. It can start running immediately and incur charges in your account.
Disable future scheduled runs; runs already started remain running.
Permanently delete a managed schedule after explicit confirmation.
Read a schedule in your connected account.
Update a managed schedule; future runs may execute different code.
List schedules in your connected account, with at most 100 rows per page.
Create a record, which may contain personal data, in a table of your connected workflow account.
Permanently delete one record, including any personal data it contains, from your connected workflow account.
Replace the entire record, including any personal data; omitted fields are removed or reset according to its table schema.
List records, including any stored personal data, in a table of your connected workflow account.
Create a record table in your connected workflow account; its subscription and storage fees are charged there.
Permanently delete one table and its records from your connected workflow account.
Read record-table metadata in your connected workflow account.
Update table name, record schema or storage capacity in your connected workflow account; storage fees are charged there.
List record tables in a project of your connected workflow account.
Create a tag in your connected account.
Delete this record from your connected account. Explicit confirmation is required.
Get a tag in your connected account.
Update a tag in your connected account.
List tags in your connected account.
List supported scheduling timezones.
Save a complete workflow definition. It may contain personal data and write-only secrets; parameters are never echoed. Maximum 500 steps and 1 MiB.
Create a workflow variable and read back its exact key and project to identify it. Value is write-only.
Delete this record from your connected account. Explicit confirmation is required.
Replace a variable key, value and optional project. Value is write-only.
List workflow variables. Values are omitted by default; explicitly requested values may contain personal data.
Call a public workflow webhook as a job, with at most 1 MiB of input. Ends at confirmed HTTP acceptance, never workflow completion. External workflow spending is uncapped.
Deliver signed JSON to a public HTTPS receiver as a job. Uses Standard Webhooks HMAC-SHA256 headers. Uncertain delivery is never automatically sent again.
Create an encrypted signing policy and reveal its secret once. Save the secret at your receiver before sending events.
Remove a signing policy so it cannot sign new deliveries. An already dispatched event cannot be recalled.
List webhook metadata in a project of your connected workflow account; trigger URLs and payloads are excluded.
